_: AFFORDANCE PROBE — what can an agent actually do through this CMS's MCP?
Not a drift race. Nothing is published and no HTML is scored. Each intent is
one fresh agent session against the vendor's own MCP surface, followed by a
postcondition checked against the CMS's own state. What is being measured is
the INTERFACE, not the output — which is why this needs no content port, no
publish pipeline and no parity gate, and why it ports to another vendor in
hours rather than weeks.
Every intent targets a DISTINCT page so the intents do not interfere and can
run in one pass after a single reset.
Outcome classes:
supported    postcondition met
refused      postcondition not met, and the surface returned an explicit error
silent-miss  postcondition not met, and the agent reported success anyway
`silent-miss` is the category worth building for. A refusal an agent can read
is a smaller problem than a success it cannot verify.
`expect` records what SHOULD happen for surfaces that are working as designed.
Where it is 'refused', a refusal is the correct answer and the interesting
measurement is whether the message let the agent recover.
X2 targets a root-level page on purpose. It first named a page inside the
section B1 measures, so any substrate whose agent SUCCEEDED at X2 shrank
B1's denominator and was then marked down for it — penalising the
capability rather than measuring it. Intents that mutate a scope must not
share that scope with an intent that measures it.

Every column seeds from probe/fixtures/site.json, exported once from the RIFT benchmark site, so the SITE is identical across substrates by construction rather than by inspection. Two differences were doing real damage before this: RIFT's Changelog already carried the link E2 asks an agent to add, handing RIFT a free `supported` for work it never performed; and RIFT's "Concepts" was a childless root page where the other seed had a populated section, so R2 asked one substrate to build a section and the other only to reparent a page.

E2, X1 and X2 target pages no other intent measures, and E2 asserts a link ABSENT from the fixture. An intent that mutates a page must not share it with an intent that measures it, and an intent must not be pre-satisfied by the starting state — both defects were found by running them.
